findings.element: print state — the keepsake sheet (render-b.js states.print, .b-print in b.css)
findings.problem: The keepsake is the one artifact this product makes that cannot be reflowed after it exists, and it does not fit A4. The sheet declares min-height:1123px — the author's own note says "A4 is 1123px" — and then renders 1441.78px tall at 794px wide. Printed to A4 with zero margins it makes two sheets: the break falls between "Final guest numbers · 51" and "Venue walk-through · 65", so the wedding day itself, the whole Behind you block, the typed link and the footer land on a second page that is 40 per cent blank. With a browser's default 12.7mm margins it is worse. The composition the panel has been shown in the frame — horizon left, measure right — is the @container (min-width:600px) layout and never happens on paper: at A4 width the container falls under 600px and the two columns stack, which is what causes the overrun. The reviewed object and the printed object are not the same object, and the printed one breaks mid-list.
findings.fix: Move the rule `.b-print .b-two { grid-template-columns: 220px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 48px; align-items: start; }` out of `@container (min-width: 600px)` (b.css:1111-1113) and declare it unconditionally on .b-print — the sheet is always 794px wide and never needs to stack, and removing the stacked horizon block reclaims the ~330px of overrun. Add `break-inside: avoid` to .b-print. Then assert it in interaction-check.mjs: at 794px width the print sheet's scrollHeight must be <= 1123, and `page.pdf({ format: "A4", margin: 0 })` must return exactly one page. If it still overruns, drop the print measure from ten pixels a day to eight and re-assert; the proportion between one gap and the next is unchanged.

findings.element: the moment editor below 1280px (.b-edit, position: fixed)
findings.problem: Below 1280 the editor is a 546px panel fixed over 94 per cent of the width, with no scrim, no body scroll lock and no focus containment. Tabbing past "Delete this moment" walks focus onto six row buttons lying physically underneath the panel — elementFromPoint on each of them returns the panel — so a keyboard or switch user is pressing Edit on rows they cannot see, while the panel above still names a different moment. The page also scrolls freely under it: with the sheet open, a scroll moved the plan 900px while the panel stayed pinned at y286, so the row the panel names walks off screen and the panel is left floating over unrelated content. This is the floating-object class from the defect library coming back on the surface with the least room. The behaviour gate proves Escape closes the editor and returns focus; nothing proves what the editor does while it is open.
findings.fix: Below 1280px make the editor modal. On open: record window.scrollY, set `inert` on the plan container (.b-ownerField's children other than the editor host) and `position: fixed; top: -<scrollY>px; width: 100%` on body; paint a scrim behind the panel at `background: var(--ink-46)` on ink ground and `var(--paper-46)` on paper; and wrap the panel's tab order so Tab from "Delete this moment" returns to the title field and Shift+Tab from the title field lands on "Delete this moment". On close, remove inert, clear the body offsets and restore the recorded scrollY in the same frame. Assert in interaction-check.mjs that with the editor open below 1280 no element outside .b-edit can take focus and that scrolling the window does not move the plan.

findings.element: owner bar "Publish" button, the "Live since 15 July" line beneath it, and the publish surface's "Sending comes next / Ready to send. The link is below."
findings.problem: One fact — whether these people already have this plan — is stated three ways on two screens, and the three disagree. The owner bar's loudest control says Publish; the line directly under it says "Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it"; pressing Publish lands on a surface headed "the moment it becomes theirs" that says "Ready to send." Someone who has never used a tool of this kind cannot tell from this whether the plan is already with Mara and Finn, whether pressing Publish sends something again, or whether the link they copied last week is the same link. This is the highest-stakes decision the owner makes — the moment a private plan becomes someone else's copy — and it is the one place the product is not sure what is true.
findings.fix: Derive all three strings from one `shareState()` accessor in fixture.js returning "never-shared" | "live" | "ended". When it returns "live": the bar's third control reads "The link", the surface it opens is headed "Live since 15 July" with the body "This link is already working. Anyone holding it sees the plan as it stands.", and "Copy the link" stays the only action. When it returns "never-shared": keep the present ceremony verbatim — Publish, "the moment it becomes theirs", "Sending comes next". No surface may compose its own sentence about sharing. Assert that the bar control's label and the publish surface's heading both come from shareState(), and that no state renders "Publish" and "Live since" at the same time.

findings.element: owner-empty, after "Set the day" is answered
findings.problem: The empty project asks exactly one question and says the day is the only thing needed to start. Answering it changes nothing on the page. The heading still reads "When is the day?", the field still reads "Set the day", and the whole reward is a line of text appended under the button: "The day is set. Moments come next." No count appears, no date, no today rule, no measure, nothing to press. The panel has been shown the empty project and the project in full flight and nothing in between, so the single most important transition in an owner's first five minutes — the moment a form becomes a plan — is the one state nobody has designed. "Inert text where nothing is built" explains the missing button; it does not explain a heading that still asks a question the page has already been given the answer to.
findings.fix: Add a twelfth state `owner-first` to STATES and CAPTIONS in render-core.js and build it in render-b.js as the answered empty project: the real horizon (the count, "Saturday 3 October 2026", "Wedding day"), the "TODAY IS 16 JULY" rule, and an empty measure headed "DAYS AWAY" carrying one line — "Nothing between today and the day yet." — with the bar now showing "Add a moment". Make submitting the empty form render that state rather than appending a sentence, so the heading "When is the day?" is replaced rather than contradicted. Capture it at 1440x960 and 390x844 and add it to the frame list.

findings.element: shell.css, b.css, lock.md — the thing Home, Notes and Tasks are meant to wear next
findings.problem: The atoms extract cleanly and they are good: shell.css already holds a nine-step ink and paper alpha ladder, leading bound to role rather than to size (--lead-label through --lead-display), a tracking ladder that moves with it, an eight-step spacing ladder from --gap-hair to --gap-page, and three durations against one easing. Above the atoms there is nothing to inherit. Every composed object is one of 101 single-use classes named after wedding nouns — .b-behindOffRow, .b-dayNowTitle, .b-unfurlMeta, .b-ogWho — and lock.md records Timeline decisions ("the day is a horizon that never moves", "editing is moving something nearer"), not language rules. A builder starting Notes could take the ladders and would then rebuild the field, the rail, the plate, the mono micro-label, the title-over-date pair, the reversibility bar and the summary-plus-disclosure fold from scratch, with no written rule for when any of them is used. Nothing has a name, so nothing can be asked for by name, and the honest answer to the round's question is that a second product cannot be built from this without copying this one.
findings.fix: Write LANGUAGE.md beside lock.md naming the eight materials this work actually invented, and lift each into a product-neutral class in shell.css: field (the ground a surface stands on, with its page ladder), rail (the measured spine — origin rule, hollow tick, filled tick for the next thing), plate (the raised ground the link card sits on), stamp (mono uppercase micro-label, sentence-case in the DOM), reading pair (title over mono date), reversibility bar (one travelling live region that names its key and falls silent), fold (one true sentence plus a disclosure that lists in full), horizon (figure, unit, date, name, in that order). For each give the rule for when it is used, the ladder values it may draw on, and one frame. Prove it by rebuilding one Notes screen from LANGUAGE.md alone with no .b-* class in it, and put that screen in the vault as the evidence.

biggestWin: The guest artifact on a phone. Seven moments, 1682 pixels, one idea: the distance to the day is the page, and the gaps between things are the real gaps. It opens on the count, the date and the name of the day in that order, tells you what today is before it shows you any other date, and says "Nothing is planned until 1 August" in words rather than leaving you to read an absence. Nothing animates, nothing asks to be tapped, no owner chrome leaks in, and every fact on it also exists in the accessible name. Someone doing something else can take the whole thing in one hand in about four seconds, which is the entire job.
